candidates.summary: Hot path split from the clipped paths. (1) The flipped viewport check is the unflipped one's inline 16-bit compare (no JSR/RTS to check_mover_x_against_viewport_left). (2) STY &CE / STX &CF are stored only on the flipped clip path, the only reader (plot_mover_sprite overwrites &CE/&CF next). (3) The unflipped hot path falls through (BCC not taken) into a tail that ends in RTS, with no LDY columns_to_clip_from_left / BEQ; the clipped paths (JSR clip_*) go to a common tail that calls the same code as a subroutine, then loads Y = columns_to_clip_from_left and falls into the existing adjust loop (BEQ dropped: a clip always leaves it >= 1). Overlaps candidate 2 (alternative: candidate 2 is the flipped part only); composes with candidate 3 only if room (+7 B here, +4 B there: the um_next ASSERT allows +8 in all, so it will not fit). Measured on a scratch build (unshifted DEBUG_LIVES, seed 1, 1000 passes from 500): logic cycles a pass 8639 -> 8592 (-47); passlock vs control 3000 passes, state and screen identical.
candidates.equivalence: Callers: only JSR get_mover_sprite_and_screen_addresses (x2, via STZ columns_to_clip_from_left) and JSR get_sprite_and_screen_addresses_for_frame_A (preceded by STZ sprite_data_offset = &CD, the same byte); each then uses AX only (plot_mover_sprite STA/STX at once; subtract_Y_rows_from_screen_address_in_AX takes AX, with LDY y_offset before it), so Y on exit (now mover, was 0) and C/N/Z/V on exit are dead. HOT PATHS: &CD (columns_to_clip_from_left) is 0 on every entry to the unclipped tail: it is zeroed at each entry (STZ at get_mover_sprite_and_screen_addresses, STZ sprite_data_offset before the third part) and nothing writes &CD between that and here unless a clip JSR runs; so the old BEQ always branched and the old exit was just STY/STX/LDY mover/LDX/LDA/RTS with AX = screen address: identical A and X, and the same two stores to unpack_column_of_sprite+1/+2 (Y = sprite address low, X = high, as before). Unflipped: the 16-bit compare is unchanged; BCS taken becomes BCC not taken falling to the tail (C=1 on both). Flipped: old check_mover_x_against_viewport_left gives C = (mover_x16 >= viewport_left16) as CMP high / (if equal) CMP low; the inline LDA low/CMP low/LDA high/SBC high gives exactly that C (the unflipped path's own identity). X and Y are unchanged by the compare (only A changes), so the sprite address in Y/X is as the old code had it. &CE/&CF: old code stored Y/X there on the flipped path; they are read only by clip_flipped_mover_loop (LDA &CE, SBC (&CE), DEC &CF, LDY &CE, LDX &CF); after return plot_mover_sprite's STA screen_address_low / STX screen_address_high (the same bytes) is the next access (via subtract_Y_rows/rows_up/add_delta, which use A, X, Y and their own bytes only), so the store moves onto the clip path, before the JSR, with the same values (Y=lo, X=hi). CLIPPED PATHS: clip_unflipped_mover_loop (JSR; returns C=1, Y/X the clipped address, columns_to_clip_from_left = n) and clip_flipped_mover_loop (same) both reach .ssa_clipped_cb1: JSR set_sprite_address does the same two stores and the same LDY mover/LDX/LDA, RTS back (stack +2 bytes, JSR/RTS only), then LDY columns_to_clip_from_left and the adjust loop as before. The one change: the old BEQ leave_1f55 (columns = 0) is gone. columns is never 0 on a clip path: a clip means mover_x < viewport_left in 16 bits, edge_x_low = viewport_left_low (set at the top of plot_mover), check_if_mover_is_on_screen had passed (x + width + 1 > viewport_left, width <= 11 per mover_types_width_table), so left - x is in 1..12 and its low byte is not 0; the clip loops therefore count n >= 1 (flipped: edge_x_low - mover_x_low != 0, so no early BEQ leave_with_sprite_address_and_carry_set). Parts 2 and 3 use the same x (mover_x_low reloaded from movers_x_low,Y). After the adjust loop it stores columns_to_clip_from_left = 0, delta_high, delta_low as before (outside the window, unchanged).
candidates.relies_on: Relies on: (a) columns_to_clip_from_left = 0 whenever no clip JSR ran (zeroed on every entry to this code, no writer between); (b) a clip leaves it >= 1 (see above; width table max &0B, sprite_column_count max &0C); (c) no caller uses Y, C, N, Z or V from this routine, nor &CE/&CF as it left them (read the three callers); (d) is_unflipped_1f14, is_flipped_1f25, set_sprite_address and leave_1f55 are referenced only in game.6502 and tools/pccats.py's profile categories (set_sprite_address keeps its name); leave_1f55 becomes unreferenced (still defined, RTS). Labels new here: ssa_unflipped_clip_cb1, ssa_clipped_cb1. Layout: +7 bytes (the um_next ASSERT HI(um_next-1)==HI(um_next+8) near game.6502:3410 allows a slide of at most +8 bytes in every non-gameplay build: um_next is at &23EF-&23F7 before, &23F6 after; +9 failed to assemble). All the window's code stays in page &1B (&1B82-&1BD2, every branch same page); check_mover_x_against_viewport_left becomes dead code outside the window (11 bytes). Later code slides 7 bytes; measured whole-pass logic cycles -47 in the scratch unshifted DEBUG_LIVES build, so no hot page crossing was introduced there (the gameplay build was not profiled).

candidates.equivalence: Flipped path: old code did STZ; LDY lo,X; STY &CE; LDA hi,X; TAX; STX &CF; JSR check_mover_x_against_viewport_left; BCS set_sprite_address; JSR clip_flipped_mover_loop. New: the same loads (Y = lo, X = hi at the compare), then LDA mover_x_low / CMP viewport_left_low / LDA &C5 / SBC viewport_left_high: C = mover_x16 >= viewport_left16, exactly what the subroutine returned (CMP high, BNE: C from the high compare; else CMP low); only A is changed, as in the subroutine. BCS set_sprite_address as before; on the clip path STY &CE / STX &CF are stored with the same values just before JSR clip_flipped_mover_loop (which reads &CE/&CF, and nothing before it did). candidates.summary: The clipped-columns loop (Y columns of +8, 12 at most) becomes one add: A + 8*Y, one INX/wrap check (8*Y <= 96, so at most one carry), then LDY #0 / STY columns as the loop left them. Independent of candidates 1 and 2 (lines 2097-2107 only), but the um_next ASSERT allows +8 bytes in all, so with candidate 1 (+7) or 2 (+5) it will not fit. +4 bytes. Measured on a scratch build: logic cycles a pass 8639 -> 8625 (-14); passlock 3000 passes, state and screen identical.
candidates.equivalence: Old loop, Y = n >= 1 times: A += 8 (low byte), on a carry X += 1 and X = &40 if that makes it &80 or more. New: A = A + 8*n in one ADC: C = 0 after ASL A x3 because 8*n <= 96 (n <= 12, see relies_on), so the ADC can carry out at most once, which is the sum of the old loop's carries (a second carry would need 8n >= 256); the wrap test (INX, BPL, LDX #&40) is then taken once, exactly as the single old carry. Without a carry X is untouched, as before. Exit: Y = 0 (LDY #0), columns_to_clip_from_left = 0, as the old DEY loop left them; what follows (STY delta_high, LDY #8, STY delta_low) is unchanged and overwrites delta_low, which this code uses as scratch for the old A (nothing reads delta_low in between: game zero page, not touched by the interrupt). Flags at exit are dead (LDY #8 follows). A, X on exit are the screen address as before.
candidates.relies_on: Relies on n = columns_to_clip_from_left <= 31 (here <= 12): a clip means mover_x < viewport_left (16 bits) and check_if_mover_is_on_screen bounded x + width + 1 > viewport_left with width <= &0B (mover_types_width_table), so n <= 12 (sprite_column_count max is &0C). Entered with Y >= 1 only (by the BEQ's fall-through; with candidate 1 applied, by the fall-through from LDY columns, also >= 1). adjust_screen_address_loop and adjust_same_page keep their names (not referenced elsewhere); delta_low scratch use. +4 bytes (um_next ASSERT allows +8 total); no page crossing in the window (&1B82-&1BD0 stays in page &1B), the later code slides 4 bytes (measured -14).
